doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Noble Sissle lets him into Broadway: 'Alive and Kicking' and 'Guys and Dolls'
summary: Sissle released Wilder to do his first Broadway show, a revue, and then 'Guys and Dolls', followed by 'Silk Stockings' and 'A Most Happy Fella' before ABC.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Noble Sissle if I could get out to go do this, because you were required to give two weeks notice to the employer you were working for, and they were getting the show together in less than the two weeks. So I asked him and he said, “well you know there are no black musicians playing in the Broadway theater, and maybe this will be a nice chance to get started.” So he said, “okay young man you can go,” he said, “I’ll give you five weeks” or something like that. “And after that I have to get somebody to replace you.” So I thought that was fair. And the show closed after seven, but he still let me come back. And shortly thereafter I got another call to do another show that turned out to be “Guys and Dolls.” And so he said, “well now I’m going to do the same thing. After five weeks, if you’re not back I have to get someone else.” And that show went three years. So I was lucky. But it was thanks to him that I got the chance to do it.
That first show you did, that must have been quite a switch.

It was. It was a revue too, by the way. It wasn’t a show with a format like “Guys and Dolls” or something like that. And they kept changing the material. Every day they would change. They went seven weeks, but for seven weeks of complete changing all the time, and it never did meld together too well, that’s why it failed. It was an interesting experience really.
Wow, and then you did one show for three years.

“Guys and Dolls.” And that was considered a long run, three years. And then when we got around I did “Silk Stockings” and “A Most Happy Fella,” and then during “A Most Happy Fella,” before that was over I went on staff at ABC. But those were good shows.
